$comment: The published site's public URL contract. Asserted against the fully assembled tree by `pnpm urls:check` (scripts/url-contract.mjs) as a required merge gate. `{version}` is substituted with the current docs major.minor; a trailing `/` resolves to that directory's index.html. `owner` names the subtree owner from the publishing ownership table: the job permitted to write that path. Adding, moving or retiring a public URL is an edit to this file, reviewed as such.

urls.note: The front door. A hand-written static page, served directly rather than redirecting anywhere, and the canonical URL for the project as a whole.
The not-found page the static host serves for every unmatched path. Retired documentation URLs land here by design; nothing is redirected.
The playground: the full-featured interactive application for trying manifests, plugins and settings. Unversioned — always the current build of the workspace.

The bare content-state viewer application: a viewer with no playground chrome, driven entirely by the content state in the URL. This path previously served the playground, which now lives at /demo/. The path is preserved rather than moved because IIIF cookbook recipes link it directly, so the URL must keep resolving even though what it serves has changed.
The documentation home for one major.minor line. Published version directories are immutable: a later release publishes alongside this one rather than over it.
The Svelte consumer example for this release, proving the framework component's packaging works in a browser.
The web-component consumer example for this release, loading the element bundle from the sibling dist/ directory.
The no-build, plain-HTML consumer example for this release; its relative ../dist/ reference is what pins the bundle location below.
The self-contained element bundle for this release, inside the version directory so an example page always loads the build its own documentation describes.
A stable alias forwarding to the newest documentation version. Safe to share in prose that should not name a version.
The human-browsable index of every published documentation version, regenerated on each publish from the version directories present in the tree.
The machine-readable version index the documentation's version switcher reads. Newest first, with the latest release carrying the "latest" alias.

The site-wide sitemap. It names the landing page, the playground, the bare viewer and the current documentation version only; archived versions are absent here and carry a noindex in the directory itself, so what is offered for indexing and what is allowed to be indexed say the same thing.

The crawl policy. It points crawlers at the sitemap and disallows nothing on purpose: a Disallow on an archived version directory would stop crawlers reading the noindex inside it, which is the only thing that gets an already-indexed archived page out of the results.

The social preview image every documentation page's og:image points at. Unversioned and suffix-stamped because scrapers cache preview images by URL for weeks; renaming it invalidates that cache, moving it breaks every card already in circulation.
The social preview image the landing page's og:image points at. Same cache contract as the documentation card, and hardcoded absolutely in apps/landing/index.html.
The social preview image the playground's og:image points at, showing the viewer actually running. Same cache contract as the other two cards, and hardcoded absolutely in apps/demo/index.html.
